title: Approved forest operations plan for the land

value: Yes
Partly

An agreement holder: a forest licence, tree farm licence, timber licence or major licence to cut, or a community forest agreement or First Nations woodland licence over 1 200 ha of Crown land (800 ha in the Coast Forest Region)
BC Timber Sales, the timber sales manager

finding: In a forest landscape area the holder of an agreement may not apply for a cutting or road permit, harvest or build a road on the land, and BC Timber Sales may not offer a timber sale licence, issue a road permit or contract logging authorization or build the road, unless it holds an approved forest operations plan that applies to the land.

actions.description: Prepare the forest operations plan, or an amendment that brings the land into its forest operations area, take it through engagement and public review, and have the minister approve it before applying, harvesting or building road.

exceptions.label: Harvest or road construction under a cutting or road permit issued before the forest operations plan that applied to the area expired, or before the holder was removed from it (§2.35(4); not an application for a new permit)
evidence: The permit and its issue date
The plan's expiry or the holder's removal

exceptions.label: Harvest or road construction under a cutting or road permit issued before the forest stewardship plan whose forest development unit contained the area expired, or before the holder left it (§2.49)
evidence: The permit and its issue date
The forest stewardship plan's expiry or the holder's removal

exceptions.label: The holder only harvests to eliminate a safety hazard, to collect seed leaving an opening of 1 ha or less, removes felled trees from landings and road rights of way, harvests up to 500 m³ the minister considers at risk from insects, fire or disease or treated to trap pests, or harvests or builds road for a prescribed purpose (§2.35(5))
evidence: The purpose, and the volume or opening
For the 500 m³ purpose, the minister's opinion

exceptions.label: The land is in a new forest landscape area, the holder's forest stewardship plan for it was approved, or submitted, before the forest landscape plan took effect, and it is within a year of that date, or the holder submitted a forest operations plan within 6 months and the minister has not yet decided it (§2.48(3)–(4))
evidence: The forest landscape plan and the date it took effect
The forest stewardship plan's approval or submission date
Any forest operations plan submitted for the portion, with its date

title: The block in the forest operations plan

value: Yes
Partly

An agreement holder: a forest licence, tree farm licence, timber licence or major licence to cut, or a community forest agreement or First Nations woodland licence over 1 200 ha of Crown land (800 ha in the Coast Forest Region)
BC Timber Sales, the timber sales manager

finding: A forest operations plan's map must show each proposed cutblock the holder intends to apply for a cutting permit for during the plan's term, or BC Timber Sales intends to include in a timber sale licence; the plan lists each one under a unique name, number or code (FPPR §4.11). This block is not in it.

actions.description: Add the block to the plan by an amendment, with its own engagement and public review, and apply only once the amendment is in effect.

title: Amendment that added the block

value: Yes
Partly

An agreement holder: a forest licence, tree farm licence, timber licence or major licence to cut, or a community forest agreement or First Nations woodland licence over 1 200 ha of Crown land (800 ha in the Coast Forest Region)
BC Timber Sales, the timber sales manager

when.value: By an amendment not yet approved or not yet in effect

finding: An amendment to a forest operations plan is not effective until the minister approves it, or, for one that needs no approval under FPPR §4.43, until 30 days after its documents reach the minister, if the minister does not require approval (FPPR §§4.44–4.45). Until then the block is not in the plan.

actions.description: Check the amendment's approval, or the date its §4.44 documents reached the minister and any §4.45 determination, before relying on it.

title: Commencement year in the plan

value: Yes
Partly

An agreement holder: a forest licence, tree farm licence, timber licence or major licence to cut, or a community forest agreement or First Nations woodland licence over 1 200 ha of Crown land (800 ha in the Coast Forest Region)
BC Timber Sales, the timber sales manager

finding: A forest operations plan must give, for each proposed cutblock, the year the holder proposes to begin harvesting it, and its map must show that year (for BC Timber Sales, the year it intends to invite applications; FPPR §4.19(1)). The plan gives none for this block.

actions.description: Have the plan amended to give the block's commencement year before scheduling it.

title: Annual forest development schedule

value: Yes
Partly

An agreement holder: a forest licence, tree farm licence, timber licence or major licence to cut, or a community forest agreement or First Nations woodland licence over 1 200 ha of Crown land (800 ha in the Coast Forest Region)
BC Timber Sales, the timber sales manager

finding: By December 31 each year the holder must make public a forest development schedule showing each location where it intends to start harvesting or building roads in the next calendar year (BC Timber Sales: each location in a timber sale licence it intends to invite applications for, or a contract logging authorization it intends to issue). The schedule for the year harvest is to start does not show the block.

actions.description: Find the schedule published for the year harvest is to start and record whether it shows the block; plan the start for a year whose schedule does, or record why it was left off.

title: Start year against the plan

value: Yes
Partly

An agreement holder: a forest licence, tree farm licence, timber licence or major licence to cut, or a community forest agreement or First Nations woodland licence over 1 200 ha of Crown land (800 ha in the Coast Forest Region)
BC Timber Sales, the timber sales manager

finding: The annual forest development schedule must be consistent with the forest operations plan, and the year harvest is to start differs from the year the plan gives for the block (FPPR §4.12). The law sets no other bar on the year itself.

actions.description: Compare the start year with the plan's. Amend the plan's year before the block goes on a schedule for another year, or record why the schedule stays consistent with the plan.

title: Public review period

value: Yes
Partly

An agreement holder: a forest licence, tree farm licence, timber licence or major licence to cut, or a community forest agreement or First Nations woodland licence over 1 200 ha of Crown land (800 ha in the Coast Forest Region)
BC Timber Sales, the timber sales manager
In the plan as the minister approved it
By an amendment the minister approved

when.value: By an amendment that needs no approval (FPPR §4.43), now in effect

finding: The plan, or an amendment that needs the minister's approval, must be publicly available for review and comment for 60 days (FPPR §4.33(1)); an amendment that needs no approval under §4.43, for 30 days (§4.34(1)). The period that put the block in the plan ran shorter.

actions.description: Count the days the plan or amendment was available. File the minister's authorization of the shorter period, or run the review again for the full period before relying on the plan or amendment.

exceptions.label: The minister authorized a shorter period of at least 10 days, satisfied that the full period would likely harm the proper management and conservation of forests and forest ecosystems, or raise the risk of wildfire or to public safety (§4.33(2), §4.34(2))
evidence: The minister's authorization of the shorter period and its grounds

title: Notice of the review period

value: Yes
Partly

An agreement holder: a forest licence, tree farm licence, timber licence or major licence to cut, or a community forest agreement or First Nations woodland licence over 1 200 ha of Crown land (800 ha in the Coast Forest Region)
BC Timber Sales, the timber sales manager

finding: Notice of the review and comment period must be published on a website kept by or for the holder and in a newspaper published in British Columbia and circulating in the plan's area, or in the Gazette.

actions.description: Record both notices and their dates; publish the missing one and run the period again from it.

title: Notice to rights holders

value: Yes
Partly

An agreement holder: a forest licence, tree farm licence, timber licence or major licence to cut, or a community forest agreement or First Nations woodland licence over 1 200 ha of Crown land (800 ha in the Coast Forest Region)
BC Timber Sales, the timber sales manager

finding: Notice of the forest operations plan, or of the amendment that added the block, must be given to each person whose rights it is likely to affect.

actions.description: List the tenures and other rights in and near the block (range, traplines, guide outfitters, water licences, woodlots and others), record who was given notice and when, and give it to anyone missed.

title: More time asked by a rights holder

value: Yes
Partly

An agreement holder: a forest licence, tree farm licence, timber licence or major licence to cut, or a community forest agreement or First Nations woodland licence over 1 200 ha of Crown land (800 ha in the Coast Forest Region)
BC Timber Sales, the timber sales manager

when.value: Yes, and it was not given

finding: A person given notice who asks for more time to review and comment must be given an extension, up to a total review and comment period of 60 days.

actions.description: Record the request and give the extension, up to 60 days in all, before the plan or amendment is relied on.

title: Engagement with Indigenous nations

value: Yes
Partly

An agreement holder: a forest licence, tree farm licence, timber licence or major licence to cut, or a community forest agreement or First Nations woodland licence over 1 200 ha of Crown land (800 ha in the Coast Forest Region)
BC Timber Sales, the timber sales manager

finding: A forest operations plan or amendment may not go to the minister unless the holder has made reasonable efforts to engage the Indigenous nations it affects, as FPPR §§4.24–4.29 set out, and its submission summarizes that engagement and the changes made for it.

actions.description: Record the nations engaged, the information given at the start (FPPR §4.25), the offer to meet (§4.28), the deadlines and the record sent to the minister (§4.29).

exceptions.label: The minister asked for the plan or amendment to be resubmitted with changes and relieved the holder of the engagement and review steps for that resubmission (§2.38(3))
evidence: The minister's request and the relief given

title: Site level plan before harvest

value: Yes
Partly

An agreement holder: a forest licence, tree farm licence, timber licence or major licence to cut, or a community forest agreement or First Nations woodland licence over 1 200 ha of Crown land (800 ha in the Coast Forest Region)
BC Timber Sales, the timber sales manager

finding: Unless the regulations provide otherwise, the holder of a forest operations plan must prepare a site level plan for the cutblock before harvest starts, identifying the approximate locations of cutblocks and roads and consistent with the forest landscape plan and the forest operations plan.

actions.description: Prepare the site level plan with what FPPR §4.55 lists and keep it until the block's obligations are complete (§4.57).

exceptions.label: Harvest only to eliminate a safety hazard, to collect seed leaving an opening of 1 ha or less, of 50 m³ or less, or restricted to removing felled trees from landings and road rights of way, Range Act grazing or hay land, experiments, recreation sites and trails, trap trees, intermediate cuts such as commercial thinning, or special forest products (FPPR §4.59)
evidence: The purpose and, where it counts, the volume or opening

title: The plan's requirements for the block

value: Yes
Partly

An agreement holder: a forest licence, tree farm licence, timber licence or major licence to cut, or a community forest agreement or First Nations woodland licence over 1 200 ha of Crown land (800 ha in the Coast Forest Region)
BC Timber Sales, the timber sales manager

finding: The holder of a forest operations plan must comply with the requirements included in it and the provisions that relate to them; on these answers the block's design does not.

actions.description: Name each requirement the block falls short of, as the plan read when the permit was issued (FRPA §20.23), and change the design or amend the plan before harvest.
